question.text: The tax treatment of profit from commodity derivatives trading that is considered as 'non-speculative business' is:

answer.text: Normal business income — can be set off against other business losses and carried forward under general business loss rules

explanation.text: The Logic: Profit from commodity derivatives that is characterised as a non-speculative business activity (typically genuine hedging of underlying business risk) is, under the conventional reading of the Income-tax Act, treated as ordinary business income. It is therefore taxed at the assessee's normal applicable rates, can be set off against other business income/losses under the general business-loss rules, and any unabsorbed non-speculative business loss can be carried forward under the standard business-loss carry-forward regime. The Trap: There is no special 15% flat rate for non-speculative commodity derivative profits, the profits are not exempt from tax, and they are not characterised as capital gains taxable at 20%. Those answers conflate concessional securities-transaction regimes or capital-asset tax with what is fundamentally treated as business income. Note: The Series XVI workbook pages cited (p.180-p.190) discuss accounting treatment, CTT, stamp duty, SEBI turnover fees and GST, but do not directly support the specific income-tax characterisation of non-speculative commodity derivative profits or the general business loss set-off/carry-forward rules. The framing above relies on general Indian income-tax knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
